title: OPS Prompt
description: A validated task contract: intent, context, constraints, ordered actions, expected outputs and the checks that decide completion. The reusable definition only; what happened during a run lives in a worklog entry. Semantics that a schema cannot express (agent resolution, path resolution, identifier uniqueness, requirement coverage) are defined in .guides/ops-contract.md and enforced by tools/ops-validate.

$schema.description: Optional editor hint. When present it must lead to this schema: either its $id, or a path relative to the prompt file that holds an identical copy.

apiVersion.description: Names the artifact family. It is not a release number and does not decide validity; this schema does.

id.description: Stable identifier, unique among the prompts of a repository.

version.description: Content revision of this prompt. Increment when the task definition changes in substance.

agent.description: Id of the execution profile this task is written for. It must resolve in the repository's agent map. Declaring it does not start a process, create a subagent, or grant permissions.

objective.description: The intent: what must be true when the task is done, stated so that someone can check it.

context.description: Facts the executor needs before acting: where the work lives, how it is built and tested, what is already known.

workspace.description: Task workspace, relative to the repository root and starting with './'. Default './'. Commands run here; inputs and outputs resolve here; the task changes nothing outside it except its own worklog entry.

inputs.description: Files or directories, relative to the workspace, that the task reads and that must exist before execution.

dependencies.description: Preconditions in plain language: tools, access, prior work.

constraints.description: Limits on scope and method that hold for the whole task.

requirements.description: Optional numbered requirements. When declared, every requirement must be covered by at least one verification check.

steps.description: Ordered units of work. Steps run in the order written.

items.description: One action in imperative natural language.

output.description: Expected artifacts. May be empty when the result is only a state that the verification checks observe.

file.description: Path relative to the workspace. A '<name>' segment marks a value chosen during execution; the worklog entry then states the concrete path.

verification.description: The checks that decide completion. The task is complete only when every check passes against the final state of the workspace.

expect.description: The observable condition that must hold.

run.description: Command that decides the check, run in the workspace. Exit code 0 means pass. Without it, the executor states how the condition was observed.

stopConditions.description: Situations in which the executor stops and reports instead of continuing.

repairAttempts.description: Maximum number of repair cycles for one failing check: a change made because that check failed, followed by re-running it. The count restarts when the check passes. Default 2. When a check still fails after that many cycles, the run stops as blocked.

timeBudgetMinutes.description: Wall-clock budget for one run, in minutes, measured by the executor. When exceeded at a step boundary, the run stops as blocked. It is not a process timeout.

createdBy.description: Who authored the definition: a person, a team, or a tool.
